reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a payment-linked Bitcoin-mining arrangement and claims participants can receive Bitcoin or passive income, including immediate and daily withdrawals. It also promotes the possibility of very large sums and asks new people to join a distributor chain. The records do not establish actual payments, contract terms, or viewer losses.

citations.quote: I pay them money, and now they mine bitcoin for me and I get some bitcoin.
You get paid every single day here.
We are buying more and more equipment and are mine bitcoin more and more.
I started working on a compliance compensation plan
We want lots and lots and lots of new people to join

opening.argument: The speaker says he tries to show material people can look up themselves rather than asking them to trust his story, and describes a full presentation as showing websites and facts. That supports reading this as a company presentation inviting scrutiny, not a promise whose truth the audience is told to take on faith. The excerpts contain optimistic claims, but do not state a guaranteed return or establish that any viewer was promised a particular outcome.

citations.quote: because I try not to tell a story I try to show facts and things that can look up on their own and they don't trust anything I say
When I do a full presentation, I show a lot of websites

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's selected quotations establish that mining, payments, and recruitment are discussed, but not that a return is guaranteed. “You get paid every single day” is a promotional assertion, not proof of a fixed yield or an instruction to send money. The presentation also says the speaker wants material viewers can check independently, a context the prosecution's summary omits.

citations.quote: You get paid every single day here.
things that can look up on their own

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An invitation to check claims does not supply the promised verification, and the speaker's stated preference for showing facts is not evidence that this presentation actually substantiates its payment claims. In the same presentation, participants are told they get paid daily and the operation is said to expand its mining equipment; those claims make this more than a neutral invitation to research.

citations.quote: You get paid every single day here.
We are buying more and more equipment

opening.argument: The video is framed as a story about the company's creation and development, with the founder recounting how he encountered Bitcoin mining and how the venture took shape. He says he initially did not know what Bitcoin or mining was, and describes the presentation as a chance to explain the company's history and vision. That is consistent with an informational founder presentation; the supplied excerpts do not show a viewer being directed through a purchase or account setup.

citations.quote: How about this. How do I talk to you guys about how bitclub network got started?
I didn't know what Bitcoin was. How it worked. I didn't know what Bitcoin mining was.
we will hear the story and the prehistory

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the mining and payment discussion as the whole function of the video, but the excerpts also show a founder explaining the company's origin and his understanding of Bitcoin. A compensation plan is mentioned, yet the supplied material does not show its terms or a specific payment request. That leaves room to read the video as an account of a business model rather than proof of a deceptive transaction.

citations.quote: I started working on a compliance compensation plan
How about this. How do I talk to you guys about how bitclub network got started?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The origin story is delivered in a favorable company presentation, not an independent lesson about Bitcoin. The speaker moves from that story to describing paid mining, daily payments, and a desire for many more people to join. Calling the presentation educational does not change the substance of those promotional claims.

citations.quote: I pay them money, and now they mine bitcoin for me and I get some bitcoin.
We want lots and lots and lots of new people to join

opening.argument: The material can be read as promotion of a mining-related business and its proposed services. The speaker describes a mining operation, equipment, and a pool, but the supplied excerpts do not lay out a guaranteed return, a required deposit amount, or a specific recruitment-based payout formula. The prosecution acknowledges that the records do not establish actual payments or contract terms. Those gaps counsel against treating the presentation alone as proof of a deceptive mechanism.

citations.quote: was starting a Bitcoin mining pool
We are buying more and more equipment
There can be many different type of revenue streams in the world Bitcoin and blockchain technology

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a paid-mining description and a distributor chain, but does not show that the quoted mining income depends on recruitment or that any specific return was guaranteed. The speaker distinguishes expansion of the mining operation from growth in membership. Without the terms of entry or payout, the excerpts leave the proposed mechanism incomplete.

citations.quote: And I don't mean our members. I mean our mining operation.
we want new people to join us, because we are building a big chain of distributors

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The speaker himself connects paying money to mining Bitcoin for the participant, then claims members are paid daily and emphasizes recruiting more people into a distributor chain. The absence of a stated deposit amount or full contract does not erase that payment-linked mining offer; it limits what can be concluded about its details, not what the video promotes.
